root_cause.text: The dm-verity FEC code in `fec_decode_bufs()` incorrectly assumed each Reed-Solomon parity codeword started and ended within a single parity block, so when `v->fec->roots` and the allocated buffer count caused a codeword to straddle a block boundary it copied past the end of the current `dm_bufio` parity block buffer and read out of bounds.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE text says `fec_decode_bufs()` “assumes that the parity bytes of the first RS codeword it decodes are never split across parity blocks” and gives a concrete OOB case where only 16 bytes remain in the block but 17 parity bytes are needed; the patch removes the old `fec_read_parity()` logic and replaces it with explicit split-aware copying using `to_copy = min(v->fec->io_size - parity_pos, v->fec->roots)` and reading the next parity block when needed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the FEC parity-read helper from the dm-verity implementation.
intent_record.what: The entire static inline function `fec_read_parity()` was deleted, including its comment, local variables, parity block calculation, buffer read via `dm_bufio_read_with_ioprio()`, and error logging/cleanup path.
intent_record.how: After this change, the codebase no longer contains this dedicated helper for reading Reed-Solomon parity data, so any remaining callers must use a different path or the functionality has been removed entirely; runtime behavior related to parity-buffer fetching and its associated error reporting is therefore eliminated from this translation unit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix FEC parity block lookup and reading to correctly handle parity bytes that can cross block boundaries, with improved error reporting.
intent_record.what: The code in `fec_decode_bufs()` no longer calls `fec_read_parity()` and no longer uses `offset` or `par_buf_offset`; instead it declares `parity_pos`, `to_copy`, and `u64 parity_block`, computes `parity_block` from `(rsb + block_offset) * v->fec->roots`, derives `parity_pos` with a mask against `v->fec->io_size - 1`, shifts `parity_block` by `v->data_dev_block_bits`, reads parity directly with `dm_bufio_read_with_ioprio()`, and adds an error log inside the failure path before returning the error.
intent_record.how: This changes how parity data is located and fetched for FEC decoding: the function now explicitly calculates the parity block index and byte position, then reads the required block directly from bufio. It also improves diagnostics when the parity read fails. Functionally, it supports parity layouts where a codeword's parity bytes may span a block boundary, instead of relying on the previous helper’s behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix FEC parity handling to span multiple parity blocks when filling Reed-Solomon decode buffers.
intent_record.what: The code replacing a simple one-shot parity copy now computes `to_copy` from the remaining bytes in the current parity buffer, copies parity data into `par_buf` with `parity_pos` tracking progress, and if not enough bytes remain it advances to the next parity block, releases the current buffer, reads the next parity block with `dm_bufio_read_with_ioprio()`, handles read errors, and finishes filling `par_buf` before calling `decode_rs8()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, parity bytes needed for Reed-Solomon decoding are no longer assumed to be contiguous within a single buffer. The change allows parity data to span multiple parity blocks, preventing truncated parity input and enabling successful decoding when the required roots exceed the remaining bytes in the current block; it also reports and aborts on parity read failures.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove obsolete parity-buffer rollover logic from fec_decode_bufs() so parity traversal is handled elsewhere during FEC decoding.
intent_record.what: The diff removes a block of code inside fec_decode_bufs() that, after advancing block_offset, used to adjust the parity read offset, handle parity bytes split across two blocks, and conditionally release the current dm_bufio buffer and call fec_read_parity() to load the next parity block.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer performs the explicit transition to the next parity buffer when the current one is exhausted. This changes how parity data is advanced and reloaded during FEC decoding, potentially relying on different surrounding logic to manage parity traversal instead of the removed inline handling.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix FEC parity handling so Reed-Solomon decode buffers can be filled correctly across parity block boundaries.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is in dm-verity FEC parity handling, specifically the parity-read/decode path that can read past a parity block boundary. Removing the FEC parity-read helper directly affects that code path and is a plausible fix for the out-of-bounds read.

The changes directly address the dm-verity FEC parity handling bug by making Reed-Solomon decode buffers work across parity block boundaries, which is the same condition that caused the out-of-bounds read in fec_decode_bufs().

The change targets fec_decode_bufs() and removes parity-buffer rollover logic related to how parity data is traversed during FEC decoding. That is directly connected to the root cause, which was incorrect handling of codewords spanning parity block boundaries leading to out-of-bounds reads.

candidates.rationale: This loop blindly copies the remaining parity bytes from the current dm_bufio parity block without first ensuring the RS codeword stays within that block, which is the direct cause of the out-of-bounds read when a codeword straddles a parity-block boundary.

This statement reads from par[offset + j] assuming the parity bytes are contiguous within the current buffer; when the codeword crosses the end of the dm_bufio block, par[offset + j] can access past the buffer boundary.

This boundary check shows the vulnerable logic's intended but flawed handling of parity bytes crossing a block boundary; the surrounding code depended on this assumption to decide whether copying could continue safely within one buffer.
This copy reads parity bytes directly from the current block buffer into the RS parity array and is unsafe if the codeword extends past the current block end, which matches the root cause.

This reads only a single parity block at a time, and the later decode logic incorrectly assumes the entire Reed-Solomon codeword resides in that one buffer, leading to the out-of-bounds access when it does not.

vuln_statements.explanation: This loop copies the remaining parity bytes from the current parity block without verifying that the Reed-Solomon codeword stays within the dm_bufio buffer, which is the root cause of the out-of-bounds read when the codeword straddles a block boundary.

This statement directly reads parity data from the current buffer using an offset that can run past the end of the parity block when the codeword crosses a block boundary, causing the OOB read described in the vulnerability.

This boundary condition is part of the flawed logic that attempts to handle parity bytes near the end of a block, but it still relies on an incorrect single-block assumption that leads to unsafe copying across block boundaries.
This copy reads parity bytes directly from the current parity block into the RS buffer and becomes unsafe when the codeword extends beyond that block, matching the out-of-bounds read root cause.

This single-block read is the setup for the buggy decode path: later logic assumes the full Reed-Solomon codeword is contained in one dm_bufio buffer, which is what breaks when the codeword spans blocks.
